title: Blockwise allocator and deferred defrag scheduler for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and spill churn
author: Maya Chen
body: Summary: This change introduces a blockwise allocation strategy for the KV cache plus a deferred, workload-aware defragmentation scheduler to reduce memory fragmentation, decrease spillover events to disk, and stabilize tail latency under bursty workloads. Motivation: Production telemetry showed persistent small-object fragmentation in the KV cache leading to premature spillover under tenant bursts (observed in ENG-8421). Spill churn caused increased disk IO, higher p50/p95 token serving latency, and costly thrashing on multi-tenant nodes. Prior approaches (aggressive synchronous compaction) increased CPU and paused hot paths. Goals: 1) Reduce fragmentation without increasing critical-path latencies; 2) Reduce frequency and volume of spillover; 3) Keep overhead bounded on CPU and background IO; 4) Make behavior tunable per-tenant. Design: - Blockwise allocator: rather than packing variable-length entries into a global free list, the allocator reserves fixed block classes (16B/64B/256B/1KB/4KB) and places entries into per-class buckets. This reduces internal fragmentation for common small KV items and provides fast O(1) allocation paths for hot sizes. - Deferred defrag scheduler: background job that runs on per-node windows and applies three tactics: 1) live-compaction of contiguous blocks when free fraction in a region crosses a threshold; 2) tenant-aware prioritization so defrag favors tenants with high eviction pressure; 3) rate-limited rewrite to avoid IO spikes. The scheduler defers compaction if the node is under high CPU or network pressure. - Hybrid spill policy: when memory pressure persists, we now prefer spilling full contiguous blocks first to preserve locality and reduce number of spill files. Also implement hysteresis to avoid ping-pong between spill and rehydrate. - Telemetry and knobs: added metrics and runtime knobs to control block sizes, defrag thresholds, max background IO, and tenant prioritization weights. Implementation notes: - Core allocator added in cache/allocator/block_allocator.{h,cc} with a thin shim allocator for compatibility with existing cache APIs. - Defrag scheduler implemented as cache/maintenance/defrag_scheduler.{h,cc} with integration hooks into the node-level resource monitor. - Spill changes in cache/spill/spill_manager.cc: added contiguous-block spiller and hysteresis logic. - Tests: unit tests for block allocation/free, stress tests with synthetic fragmentation patterns, and integration perf tests run in benchmark-lab. Performance: - Internal benchmark on m60 instances with mixed small/large KV workload: 34% reduction in spill events, 22% reduction in average node-level spill IO, 12% improvement in p95 generation latency under burst tests. - In a 72-hour canary on a production-like cluster (10 nodes) we observed 18% lower median memory used for equivalent resident entries and a 28% reduction in spill cycle frequency. Backwards compatibility: Existing cache APIs unchanged; shim allocator defaults to legacy mode when the feature flag is off. Migration: rolling rollout recommended: enable block allocator without defrag for 48h to observe allocation profiles, then enable deferred defrag with conservative thresholds. Safety measures: feature flag, per-tenant enablement, max background IO hard cap, and safe-fallback to legacy allocator on detected anomalies. Testing & CI: unit tests added (allocator/defrag), end-to-end scenario in benchmark-lab, and a soak canary run. Some flaky stress tests (cache_stress/frag_replay) were stabilized by increasing test timeout and running on dedicated nodes. Documentation: added design rationale and operational runbook to docs/ops/kv-defrag.md. Files changed (high-level): - cache/allocator/block_allocator.h - cache/allocator/block_allocator.cc - cache/maintenance/defrag_scheduler.h - cache/maintenance/defrag_scheduler.cc - cache/spill/spill_manager.cc - docs/ops/kv-defrag.md - tests/integration/kv_block_allocator_test.cc Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag gated on main; 2) Canary on non-production region with low tenant variance for 72h; 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of nodes, monitor metrics; 4) Full rollout if no regressions. Release notes: Reduced KV cache fragmentation and spill churn by introducing a blockwise allocator with deferred defragmentation. See ENG-8421 for background.

review_comments: Leo Martínez: Can we quantify CPU overhead of defrag in worst-case? Please add a microbenchmark and a knob to cap CPU share.
Author (Maya): Added a CPU cap knob and microbenchmark results to the PR description and tests. The defrag pipeline yields <5% CPU on our worst-case repro with default thresholds.
Priya Raman: Tenant prioritization looks good but ensure it cannot starve low-priority tenants; add fairness window.
Author (Maya): Implemented fairness window (configurable) so low-priority tenants are guaranteed compaction every N cycles.
Ethan Wu: Flaky test observed on CI; rerun and increase timeout for stress replay. Verify no memory leak after forced shutdown.
Author (Maya): Fixed test harness, reran canary; leak check passes under ASAN in the canary runs. CI rerun green.
ci_checks: benchmark-lab: pass (local repros match reported improvements)
merge_details: Merged by squash-merge after approvals from Leo Martínez and Priya Raman. Commit message summarized feature, rollout instructions, and ENG ticket.
release_notes: Introduce blockwise KV allocator and deferred defragmentation scheduler. Expected benefits: lower fragmentation, fewer spill events, and improved tail latency under bursty workloads. Tunable via feature flags and runtime knobs.
notes_for_ops: Ops: enable feature flag in staging; monitor metrics: kv.cache.free_fragmentation_ratio, kv.spill.events, node.background_io, kv.defrag.cycles. Use conservative defaults for defrag thresholds in multi-tenant noisy nodes.
post_merge_actions: Create a Linear card to track the rollout (ENG-8470), schedule 72h canary, and collect spike telemetry; follow-up PR planned to add adaptive block sizing based on observed allocation histograms.
